evidence: From the station follow the footpath to the Mangawhero River Bridge and cross over onto Old Station Road.
From here the trail crosses the stream and follows the Old Coach Road through to Horopito.
It's a one way walk or ride so you'll need to return the same way or arrange transport back.

ways.label: Ohakune to Hapuawhenua Viaduct and return
evidence: Walk the historic Hapuawhenua Viaduct and enjoy both old and new viaducts and native forest surrounds.
From here you can return to Ohakune or carry on to Horopito.

access_points.name: Marshalls Road car park
access_points.quote: drive to the Marshalls Road car park (5 minutes drive from Ohakune) and begin the ride there

access_points.name: Horopito parking area off Matapuna Road
access_points.quote: Turn onto Matapuna Road from SH4. There is a parking area just across the railway line.

doubts: The start, Ohakune Railway Station, has no feature of its own; it is given the place Ohakune (T3) as the town it is in, while the track itself begins at the Marshalls Road car park (F4). The Horopito end is given as the place Horopito (T2); the Matapuna Road parking area has no clear feature (F1 on Clydes Access may or may not be it). The page says the walk can be walked back the same way or with transport, so W1 is one-way as presented. The Heritage section says the Taonui Viaduct is not open for visitor use and only a viewing side track is being restored, which conflicts with the description of following the stream to the viaduct. W2 is the 'return to Ohakune' option from Hapuawhenua Viaduct, with no time or distance given. Taonui Stream (T7) is matched by name only.
